events.title: [Practice Made Perfect Series] Word First, AI Later: Mastering Microsoft Word for Legal Documents
events.outline: A hands-on workshop on the Microsoft Word features lawyers need to draft, review and finalise legal documents accurately. Participants will learn to use Styles, automatic numbering, tables of contents and cross-references, and to fix common formatting problems. The session also covers the confidentiality risks of tracked changes, comments and hidden metadata, how to clean documents before sending them out, and why sound Word skills should come before using AI tools in drafting.

events.title: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals (SCMP) Module 1+
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Strategic Conflict Management for Professionals Module 1 is an intensive two-day training programme to learn the foundations of interest-based mediation which focuses on the disputing parties’ interests and encourages a broader range of solutions. You will learn about the nature of conflicts and the most effective techniques to manage them.

events.title: SMU-IPAS Advanced Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring Module 11: Capstone - Integrating the Concepts+
events.outline: This module will integrate and provide a coherent overview of the various insolvency and restructuring concepts, knowledge and tools taught in Modules 1 to 10 of the SMU-IPAS Graduate Certificate in Insolvency and Restructuring through a combination of lecture and case study.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Annual CPD Day 2026 (Part 2)+
events.outline: The Law Society’s 16th Annual CPD Day, first held in 2011, returns with Part 2 as live webinars on 3 and 4 November 2026. Attend either half-day or both to earn CPD and MEC points. Topics include AML, civil litigation, employment law, ESG, third party funding, sentencing updates, complaints against lawyers, and affidavit drafting.

events.title: LES Singapore Basic Licensing Course 2026+
events.outline: Understand aspects of the licensing of intellectual property (IP) – particularly for trade marks, copyright, patents, and registered designs – at the LES Singapore Basic Licensing Course 2026! Organised together with the Licensing Executives Society (Singapore), our programme will cover the various principles and procedures involved in licensing negotiations. Learn how to effectively apply them in practice, through a “hands-on” scenario.

events.title: [Practice Made Perfect Series] Smarter Calculations, Clearer Data: Microsoft Excel for Legal Professionals
events.outline: A hands-on workshop to build confidence with Microsoft Excel using data sets common in legal work. Participants will learn basic navigation, essential formulas, formatting and best practices to reduce errors in calculations such as matrimonial asset divisions and fee budgets. The session covers how to find and remove hidden data and metadata that may expose confidential or personal data, and introduces Microsoft Copilot, including the risks of using AI on client data.

events.title: [APCEL-EWBCLB Book Launch] The Oxford Handbook of Climate Change and Private Law
events.venue: Yale-NUS College Performance Hall  NUS Law (UTown), Kent Ridge Campus
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: The Oxford Handbook of Climate Change and Private Law edited by Douglas A. Kysar (Yale) and Ernest Lim (NUS) offers a comprehensive scholarly assessment of the impacts of climate change for private law. It brings together a team of world-leading experts to examine the interface between private law and climate change, including how existing private law can respond to climate change and whether private law itself might be impacted by climate change.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Data Poisoning and International Law
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore - Centre for International Law. What happens when an adversary corrupts the data that AI systems rely on? As militaries use AI for intelligence, targeting and operations, data poisoning could disrupt decisions without physical force. This CIL panel examines when such interference might breach international law, including rules on intervention, use of force, deception, perfidy and attacks during armed conflict. Experts will discuss how existing legal rules apply when data becomes both a weapon and a vulnerability.

events.title: ISCA Financial Forensics Community Engagement Session: When Things Don't Add Up
events.outline:
This event is organised by Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants. The session aims to:
- Engage the ISCA Financial Forensics community through a candid discussion on regulatory scrutiny, special audits, investigations and corporate accountability.
- Provide practical insights into how regulators, legal advisers and financial forensic practitioners view emerging concerns within listed companies.
- Explore the role of Notices of Compliance (NOCs), special audits and independent investigations when confidence in a company's governance, disclosures or conduct comes into question.
- Demonstrate the distinct role of financial forensic professionals in helping organisations establish facts, support decision-making and restore confidence.
- Build awareness of the multidisciplinary capabilities required in modern financial forensics.

events.title: Distinguished Visitor Lecture: Coded Power: How to End Digital Despotism and Reclaim Control over Our Data
events.venue: Wee Chong Jin Moot Court, NUS Law
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: “Coded power” is control over the formal systems that organise society, through law or digital code. While such power can serve its creators’ interests, digital code and data control can fragment societies and weaken social cohesion. Digital despotism is not inevitable: participatory, shared data governance can give people collective control over how their data is accessed and used.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Decarbonization of the International Maritime Sector: The IMO Regimes
events.outline: This webinar is organised by NUS - Centre for International Law. This module examines the legal, institutional, and policy foundations of maritime decarbonization. It explores the role of the IMO in regulating shipping emissions, the evolution of its climate strategy, and key regulatory measures aimed at achieving net-zero emissions. The session also considers emerging frameworks, alternative fuels, and challenges relating to equity, infrastructure, emissions accounting, and the effectiveness of international climate action in the maritime sector.

events.title: AI Workshop for Legal Professionals (5 November)
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Step into the world of artificial intelligence with this practical, in-person workshop designed specifically for legal professionals. Gain foundational skills and the confidence to apply AI in your everyday work—from legal research to drafting and contract analysis. Guided by experienced trainers, you'll explore how to evaluate and use a range of general and legal-specific AI tools effectively and responsibly. Participants will work directly on their own devices with live support, ensuring a hands-on, outcome-focused learning experience.

events.title: 15th Commercial Arbitration Symposium 2026
events.venue: The Arts House, 1 Old Parliament Lane, Singapore 179429
events.outline: The Symposium returns to the Old Parliament House, featuring participant-led discussions on current issues in commercial arbitration. With no scheduled speakers or speeches, delegates whose topics are selected will introduce them, followed by open discussions moderated by experienced co-chairs from Singapore and abroad. Topics will be grouped into themes across three working sessions, with participants encouraged to raise any relevant issues.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Sustainability Apex Programme Masterclass #11: Sustainable Supply Chain Management
events.outline: This masterclass examines sustainable supply chain management and its role in strengthening resilience, corporate accountability, and long-term value creation. Topics include responsible sourcing, supplier due diligence, traceability, scope 3 decarbonisation, and emerging regulatory developments. The session also covers procurement, contractual, disclosure, and transparency considerations relevant to managing sustainability-related issues across organisational supply networks.

events.title: LES Singapore Intermediate Licensing Course 2026
events.outline: Understand aspects of the licensing of intellectual property (IP) – particularly for trade marks, copyright, patents, and registered designs – at the LES Singapore Intermediate Licensing Course 2026! Organised together with the Licensing Executives Society (Singapore), our programme will cover the various principles and procedures involved in licensing negotiations.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Candour Counts: Guiding practice trainees through the duty of candour in Bar admission
events.outline: In this online panel discussion, experienced counsel will discuss the evolving jurisprudence on the duty of candour in admission proceedings and the principles that have emerged from recent decisions. The panellists will consider common disclosure scenarios, the role of supervising solicitors in guiding and rehabilitating trainees, and how to instil the duty of candour from the very start of a lawyer's professional journey.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Conflict or No Conflict? Lessons from PED 2026
events.outline: Conflicts of interest are among the most challenging ethical issues faced by practitioners. Drawing on Chapter 5 of the Professional Ethics Digest 2026, this webinar explores key principles governing conflicts of interest, including duties of loyalty, confidentiality and independent professional judgment. Through realistic scenarios involving clients, former clients, related entities and personal interests, examine how conflicts can arise in everyday practice and how to address them.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Football Regulation in 2027: What You Need to Know
events.outline: Participants will gain an authoritative perspective on the rationale behind these reforms and their implications for the regulation of player contracts and international transfers.

events.title: Insurance Law Forum 2026
events.venue: CapitaSpring L20 Multifunction Hall, 8 Market Street, Singapore 048948
events.outline: This event is organised by Singapore Insurance Institute. Insurance Law Forum 2026 gathers leading insurance disputes practitioners to examine recent court decisions reshaping insurance coverage and claims. Four short talks cover business interruption cover, arbitration clauses and contractual time bars, insurer and broker liability, and digital-asset recovery, followed by a moderated panel on emerging risks in fraud, cyber and AI. For claims handlers, brokers, underwriters and loss adjusters.

events.title: JLP - Advising Clients on Deal Structures
events.venue: SAL, Marina 3, The Adelphi #07-01, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: Explore ethical issues, basic deal design structures, and factors influencing deal structure. Examine contractual and cross-border issues and understand the role of deal lawyers in managing these elements.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Adjudication Insights 2026 - Recent Developments and Recurring Issues Under the Security of Payment Regime
events.outline: This seminar provides a considered update on recent adjudication determinations and review decisions under the SOP Act. Drawing on a detailed commentary of AA and ARA decisions handed down over the past year, the session examines the reasoning underlying these decisions, identifies points of divergence between adjudicators, and offers a view on where the law may be expected to develop.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Navigating Appointments, Conflicts and Fees in R&I Practice: Ethical and Professional Challenges
events.outline: Appointments, conflicts and fees raise ethical, professional and practical questions in restructuring and insolvency practice. This course will explore the considerations that arise when practitioners take on appointments, manage potential conflicts and address fee arrangements. It will consider how professional obligations and practical realities intersect, and provide a forum for reflecting on the challenges practitioners may encounter in work.

events.title: AI and Corporate Governance:  Ethics and Oversight of the AI Compliance Program
events.outline: This Masterclass is designed to give participants both the ethical grounding and the practical governance tools needed to oversee AI responsibly. Participants will leave with a working framework for advising on, building, and overseeing AI governance and compliance programs grounded in fiduciary duties, regulatory guidance, and practical implementation experience.

events.title: The Strait of Hormuz: Navigation, Sovereignty and Cooperation by Dr Reece Lewis
events.venue: Seminar Room 3-1, NUS Bukit Timah Campus, Block B, Level 3, 469 Bukit Timah Road, S259756
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore - Centre for International Law. This lecture examines coastal sovereignty and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, focusing on Oman, Iran and user States. It explores treaty and customary law, safety and environmental regulation, and the funding of maritime services. Drawing on shared cooperation in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, it considers how coastal States, shipping interests and the IMO can work together to manage this strategic waterway while safeguarding navigational rights and respecting coastal State interests.

events.title: AI Workshop for Legal Professionals (12 November)
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: Step into the world of artificial intelligence with this practical, in-person workshop designed specifically for legal professionals. Gain foundational skills and the confidence to apply AI in your everyday work—from legal research to drafting and contract analysis. Guided by experienced trainers, you'll explore how to evaluate and use a range of general and legal-specific AI tools effectively and responsibly. Participants will work directly on their own devices with live support, ensuring a hands-on, outcome-focused learning experience.

events.title: [WEBINAR & IN-PERSON] Mediation Advocacy Skills+
events.venue: Webinar / 137 Amoy Street, Far East Square, #03-06, Singapore 049965
events.outline: This event is organised by Sage Mediation Institute for Leadership Education. As mediation gains prominence, advocates must stay updated and effective, not only in the courtroom but also at the mediation table. This workshop covers the thoughtful preparation needed for an advocate to prepare the client for an international mediation and how an advocate can engage effectively with counterparties and the mediator. Advocates who complete the full workshop may accredit themselves as IMI-Certified Mediation Advocates.

events.title: When Private Harm Becomes Public Wrong: Family Violence at the Intersection of Family Law and Criminal Law
events.venue: SUSS Room at the State Courts, 1 Havelock Square, Singapore 059724
events.outline: Family violence sits astride two bodies of law with very different objects: the protective, forward-looking family law regime and the retrospective, punitive criminal law. This seminar reframes family violence as a hybrid legal problem and maps the friction points between the two regimes – thresholds for intervention, information-sharing, reporting duties and parallel proceedings. It explores how the two systems can work together to achieve balanced outcomes.

events.title: Negotiating Success+
events.venue: National University of Singapore (Kent Ridge Campus)
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: This 2-day workshop will focus on giving participants a working knowledge of the Interests-Based Model of Negotiation created by Roger Fisher and as taught at the Program on Negotiation at Harvard Law School. It will be taught through a mixture of presentations, facilitated discussions and role plays.

events.title: Accelerated Route to Membership International Arbitration (ARM)
events.outline: To provide a fast-track route to Membership through the International (i.e., non-domestic) Arbitration Pathway. The Accelerated Route to Membership has been designed for busy professionals who have some unassessed knowledge of International Arbitration. The aim of the programme is to assess whether the candidate has the knowledge required to understand the process of International Arbitration.

events.title: LawNet Training Workshop (17 November 2026)
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This training workshop guides attendees through the new features and functionalities of LawNet.com. Through walkthroughs and hands-on exercises, participants will learn how to use the revamped platform efficiently

events.title: SCL(S) Conference 2026: Technology, Legal Innovation and Singapore’s Built Future
events.venue: M Hotel Singapore, Banquet Suite at Level 10, 81 Anson Road, Singapore 079908
events.outline:
Industry leaders, legal experts & technologists examine how S'pore can harness digital innovation yet maintain robust legal safeguards. Through expert panels, case studies & debate, we explore the legal frontiers of Construction 4.0 to chart a course for continued excellence in the built environment sector. Sessions:
The Data Centre Boom
Digital Contract Administration & Claims
Digital Evidence & the Future of Construction Disputes
In AI We Trust? The Evidential Risks of Automating Project Records

events.title: SCL(S) Conference 2026: Technology, Legal Innovation and Singapore’s Built Future
events.outline: Industry leaders, legal experts & technologists examine how S'pore can harness digital innovation yet maintain robust legal safeguards. Through expert panels, case studies & debate, we explore the legal frontiers of Construction 4.0 to chart a course for continued excellence in the built environment sector. Sessions: The Data Centre Boom, Digital Contract Administration & Claims, Digital Evidence & the Future of Construction Disputes, In AI We Trust? The Evidential Risks of Automating Project Records

events.title: [WEBINAR] Specialist Arbitration Series: Cryptocurrency Arbitrations (Virtual Edition)
events.outline: The SIAC Academy Specialist Arbitration Series seeks to spotlight different areas of arbitration disputes, the major stakeholders, contractual relationships, key legal principles and types of claims and defences that are typically brought in that area, as well as the strategic considerations to note in each stage of the arbitration for that particular area of dispute. In the third instalment of this series, we focus on Cryptocurrency Disputes.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Equity’s Shifting Boundaries: Resulting Trusts, Illegality and Limitation in Recent Singapore Litigation
events.outline: This seminar examines recent developments in equity and trusts through several important decisions.

events.title: [WEBINAR] ACRA's Prescribed Anti-Money Laundering Combating the Financing of Terrorism ("AML/CFT") Course
events.outline: This event is organised by Chartered Secretaries Institute Singapore (CSIS). This course intends to equip [Registered Filing Agents (RFAs)] with the knowledge and understanding of anti-money laundering (AML) and counter financing of terrorism (CFT) to enable RFAs to comply with prevailing ACRA and relevant Singapore’s regulatory requirements.

events.title: JLP - Effective Documents and Evidence Management
events.venue: SAL, Marina 3, The Adelphi #07-01, 1 Coleman Street (S179803)
events.outline: This 1-day training equips young lawyers and in-house counsel with practical skills to manage documents and evidence effectively. Participants will learn dispute prevention strategies, evidence preservation, document management, discovery compliance, litigation readiness, and the ethical use of technology through case studies, discussions, and practical exercises.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Lecture by Professor Jakub Handrlica on “Nuclear Reactors on the Moon (and Beyond): Legal Aspects of Space Reactor Deployment”
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore - Centre for International Law. Nuclear reactors could power mining and human settlements on the Moon, but their deployment requires a clear legal framework. This lecture examines how international space law and nuclear law apply to lunar reactors and whether existing rules can address their challenges. It also explores what a future framework for “space nuclear law” might look like as nuclear energy becomes increasingly important to exploration of the Moon and beyond. The discussion considers legal gaps and future regulation.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Home Ground or Away Game? Restructuring Across Indonesia and Singapore
events.outline: This webinar explores restructuring and insolvency issues for corporate groups that have operations spread across ASEAN, focusing on Indonesia and Singapore. It will cover developments in these countries' restructuring and insolvency frameworks, including cross-border recognition of insolvency proceedings, enhanced judicial cooperation, practical challenges in cross-border restructurings, and asset recovery exercises that have come up due to the cross-border nature of modern businesses.

events.title: Mediation+
events.venue: National University of Singapore (Kent Ridge Campus)
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: This workshop will focus on giving participants a working knowledge of how mediation works, its pros and cons, the conflict resolution model used, the process and stages of mediation, learning to facilitate the resolution of a dispute and dealing with the people aspect of any dispute. The workshop will be taught through a mixture of presentations, facilitated discussions and role plays.

events.title: Mediation Advocacy (Nov 2026)+
events.outline: Mediation Advocacy is a specialised training programme designed to equip lawyers and professionals with the strategic, legal, and practical skills required to represent clients effectively in mediation. This programme focuses on how advocates can add value throughout the mediation process: from preparing clients and developing negotiation strategies, to managing dynamics during mediation sessions and achieving durable settlement outcomes.

events.title: ESG Conference
events.venue: SMU Ngee Ann Kongsi Auditorium 60 Stamford Rd, Singapore 178900
events.outline: This conference opens with a Fireside Chat with Minister Indranee Rajah, followed by expert sessions with regulators, sustainability and finance professionals and lawyers. Topics: sustainable finance beyond compliance; capital projects and infrastructure in the energy transition; carbon markets and the legal nature of carbon credits; and sustainability reporting.

events.title: Business Valuation for Litigators Module 4 – Special Cases
events.venue: Room 801, Level 8, NTUC Centre, No.1 Marina Boulevard, Singapore 018989
events.outline: This event is organised by J.S. Held. This seminar explains why commonly used income and market approach methods may be inappropriate in certain situations and demonstrates how alternative approaches, including the cost approach, option pricing model, probability-weighted expected return method, and modern DCF method, can be applied to address the challenges posed by those situations. Where possible, concepts will be illustrated through judgments and arbitral awards, making the seminar particularly relevant to disputes lawyers.

events.title: The Alabama Claims Arbitration: Lessons and Practical Insights for Today’s Treaty Negotiators, Counsel, and Arbitrators
events.venue: Conrad Singapore Orchard, 1 Cuscaden Road, Singapore 249715
events.outline: This event is organised by NUS Centre for International Law. Course participants will be exposed to historical documents such as the Treaty of Washington, the correspondence of the American and British Agents with their respective national capitals, various Protocols of the Tribunal’s Conferences, and private correspondence of various participants in the arbitration, and the diary of one of the arbitrators.

events.title: What Every Lawyer Should Know About International Tax 2026
events.outline:
As a legal counsel, it is more important than ever to have a high-level understanding of the international tax structures and concepts underpinning your clients' corporate structure and transactions.

Through this masterclass, participants will be equipped with solid insight and understanding of the relevant international tax fundamentals to holistically understand their clients' structures and considerations.

events.title: Global Rule of Law Conference 2026+
events.outline: The Global Rule of Law Conference 2026 (24-26 Nov 2026) brings together judicial leaders, policymakers, practitioners and scholars to explore how the Rule of Law shapes resilient societies and drives sustainable economic growth.

events.title: [Practice Made Perfect Series] Work Smarter: Microsoft Outlook & PowerPoint for Legal Professionals
events.outline: A two-in-one hands-on workshop on Microsoft Outlook and PowerPoint for legal practice. Participants will learn to manage email, calendars and tasks efficiently, apply settings that reduce misdirected emails and the disclosure of confidential client information, and track court dates and filing deadlines. The PowerPoint segment covers templates, layouts and visual aids, and how to protect client confidentiality in pitch and seminar decks.

events.title: APIEx Symposium 2026 - Expert Evidence in Action: From Appointment to Impact in Arbitration and Litigation
events.venue: Singapore University of Social Sciences, 463 Clementi Road, Singapore 599494
events.outline: This event is organised by Asia Pacific Institute of Experts. Expert evidence often determines the outcome in complex disputes, yet tribunals continue to criticise how experts are selected, instructed & deployed. Poorly framed instructions, blurred independence and misaligned counsel/expert expectations undermine the strongest cases. Through keynote insights, panel discussions and mock engagements, dispute professionals explore the lifecycle of expert involvement, dissect real-world pitfalls, benchmark best practices and refine the lawyer–expert interface..

events.title: Accelerated Route to Fellowship in International Arbitration+
events.outline: The Accelerated Route to Fellowship has been designed for busy professionals who have substantial unassessed knowledge and experience of International Arbitration. The aim of the programme is to assess whether the candidate has the knowledge required to apply the principles and procedure of International Arbitration using arbitration legislation based on the UNCITRAL Model Law and Arbitration Rules and is capable of writing a reasoned and enforceable International Arbitration Award.

events.title: CIL’s Dialogue with India High Commissioner Dr. Shilpak Ambule on Partners with Trust: India-Singapore Relations in a Changing World
events.venue: Lecture Theatre @ NUS, Bukit Timah Campus Block B, Level 3, 469 Bukit Timah Road, Singapore 259756
events.outline: This event is organised by NUS Centre for International Law. The 4th round of India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable, held in Singapore on 20th August 2026, underscored the commitment from both sides to forge an ever closer partnership. High Commissioner Dr. Ambule will share his thoughts on how India and Singapore are strengthening cooperation, expanding collaboration and leveraging their respective strengths and complimentarities, for the benefit of the two countries, within the framework of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Navigating Trade, Sustainability and Investment Law in the Era of Economic Security
events.outline: This seminar examines how sustainability, investment, economic security, and technological change are reshaping international economic law and legal practice.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Global and Regional AI Governance and Regulation, and the Role of Data Protection in AI
events.outline: In this 2-hour webinar, participants will be exposed to: (a) an overview of AI governance and regulation and some of the key considerations that shape it; (b) A comparative scan of AI regulatory approaches in five regions, namely US, EU, China, the rest of APAC and Singapore, as well as takeaways for Singapore; and (c) The use of data protection law as a regulatory tool for AI (especially generative AI).

events.title: LawNet Training Workshop (9 December 2026)
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This training workshop guides attendees through the new features and functionalities of LawNet.com. Through walkthroughs and hands-on exercises, participants will learn how to use the revamped platform efficiently
